issues.title: Hardcoded devtools loading message text
issues.description: The rule requires all user-facing strings to be defined in web/i18n/en-US/ translation files and accessed via useTranslation hook. The code hardcodes 'Loading devtools...' directly in the JSX instead of using a translation key.
issues.rule_name: Frontend User-Facing Strings Must Use i18n Translations

issues.title: Devtools rendered before application children causes layout issues
issues.description: The TanStackDevtoolsLoader is now rendered before the children components in the QueryClientProvider. This reverses the intended rendering order from the original PR, which had devtools after children. When devtools mount first, they may inject DOM elements before the main application content is rendered, potentially causing layout shifts, visual flashes, or z-index conflicts. Devtools should be rendered as a sibling after main content to avoid interfering with the initial application layout and rendering.

issues.title: Missing error logging in TanStack devtools lazy import
issues.description: The TanStackDevtoolsLoader silently swallows import errors without logging them, making it impossible to debug why the devtools fail to load. This creates an inconsistent error handling pattern compared to the ReactScanLoader (in the same PR), which properly logs errors with console.error before returning a fallback component. When developers encounter issues with TanStack devtools not appearing, they will have no visibility into whether it's due to an import failure, missing dependencies, or other issues.

issues.title: console.error violates Frontend Code Must Not Use console Statements rule
issues.description: The ReactScanLoader uses console.error which directly violates Rule 25 from AGENTS.md added in this same PR. The rule explicitly states that production frontend code must avoid console.log, console.warn, and console.error statements as enforced by the no-console warning rule. This creates an inconsistency where the code violates a compliance rule that was just introduced, and creates inconsistent error handling compared to TanStackDevtoolsLoader which silently catches errors. The use of console statements in production code should be replaced with proper logging mechanisms.

issues.title: console.error used in frontend code
issues.description: Rule 25 prohibits console statements in frontend code. The added code logs an error with console.error when lazy-loading fails.
issues.rule_name: Frontend Code Must Not Use console Statements

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #30318 - refactor(web): organize devtools components

structured_output.summary:
This PR moves the React Scan and TanStack devtools implementations into `web/app/components/devtools/{react-scan,tanstack}/` and adds a small `loader.tsx` per tool. Each loader returns `null` unless `IS_DEV` is true, and otherwise renders a `lazy()`-imported devtools component inside a `Suspense` boundary. `layout.tsx` now mounts `ReactScanLoader` instead of statically importing `ReactScan`, and `query-client.tsx` mounts `TanStackDevtoolsLoader` instead of inlining its own lazy import. The two renames are 100% similarity, so history is preserved. I read the moved files and checked all references; nothing in the repo still points at the old `components/react-scan` or `components/devtools` paths.

The core behavior is sound. Because the `IS_DEV` guard returns before the lazy component renders, the `import()` factory never runs in production, and react-scan is no longer pulled into the root layout's static graph. The remaining issues are small: the two loaders handle chunk-load failures differently, the loaders have no tests, the PR description mentions a barrel `index.ts` that does not exist, and the dev-only fallback text is rendered in the body.
structured_output.verdictRationale: No critical or high issues. The lazy-loading gate is correct and the import paths are fully updated. The findings are low-severity consistency, test-coverage, and documentation-accuracy issues that can be addressed in this PR or follow-ups.

architecture.overview:
Before this PR, the root layout statically imported `ReactScan` from `web/app/components/react-scan.tsx`, which pulled react-scan into the layout module graph. TanStack devtools were lazily imported inline in `web/context/query-client.tsx` from `@/app/components/devtools`, gated by `IS_DEV` at render time. Both integrations were configured in different places with different patterns.

After this PR, each tool lives in its own folder under `web/app/components/devtools/`. A per-tool `loader.tsx` owns the environment check, the `lazy()` import, and the `Suspense` boundary. The root layout and the TanStack query provider only mount the loader. The implementation files (`scan.tsx`, `tanstack/devtools.tsx`) are unchanged apart from their location, and the lazy import only resolves when `IS_DEV` is true.
steps: Entry points are `web/app/layout.tsx` (server component, mounts `<ReactScanLoader />` inside `<body>`) and `web/context/query-client.tsx` (`TanstackQueryInitializer`, mounts `<TanStackDevtoolsLoader />` inside `QueryClientProvider`).

`react-scan/loader.tsx` gates on `IS_DEV`, then lazily imports `./scan`, which calls `scan({ enabled: true, dangerouslyForceRunInProduction: true })` in an effect. A failed import logs via `console.error` and falls back to a null component.

`tanstack/loader.tsx` uses the same gate and lazy pattern to import `./devtools`, which renders `TanStackDevtools` with the React Query and Form plugins. A failed import falls back to a null component silently.
The implementation files moved without content changes (100% similarity renames), so the only behavioral differences are where the code is mounted and when the chunk is requested.
Net effect: in production neither loader triggers a dynamic import, so the devtools chunks are never requested. In development both are fetched on first render.

findings.title: TanStack loader silently swallows chunk-load failures
findings.fixPrompt: In `web/app/components/devtools/tanstack/loader.tsx`, the `.catch` on the lazy import (lines 9-11) returns a null fallback without reporting the error. Change it to accept the error and call `console.error` with a message like 'Failed to load TanStack devtools:', matching the pattern in `web/app/components/devtools/react-scan/loader.tsx` lines 9-12. Keep the null-component fallback so the app still renders when the chunk fails.

findings.title: Loader gating and fallback behavior have no tests
findings.fixPrompt: Add unit tests for `web/app/components/devtools/tanstack/loader.tsx` and `web/app/components/devtools/react-scan/loader.tsx`. Mock `@/config` so `IS_DEV` can be true or false. Cover three cases: with `IS_DEV` false, nothing renders and the dynamic `./devtools` or `./scan` import is never triggered; with `IS_DEV` true, the wrapped component renders; and when the import rejects, the loader falls back to null without crashing. Follow the conventions of existing `*.spec.tsx` files under `web/context/`. Assert on rendered output and the import being invoked, not on internal implementation details.

findings.title: PR description claims a barrel index that does not exist
findings.fixPrompt: The PR description says `web/app/components/devtools/index.ts` was simplified, but that file does not exist and the diff does not create it. Either add `web/app/components/devtools/index.ts` that re-exports `ReactScanLoader` and `TanStackDevtoolsLoader`, and update the imports in `web/app/layout.tsx` and `web/context/query-client.tsx` to use it, or edit the PR description to remove the barrel claim. Choose one; do not leave the description and code disagreeing.

findings.title: Dev-only loading text is rendered in the page body
findings.body:
The React Scan fallback renders a visible `Loading devtools...` div inside `<body>`. It only appears in development, but it renders on every dev load until the chunk arrives, and the TanStack loader uses `fallback={null}` for the same situation. The two loaders should behave the same way, and a developer-tool placeholder does not need visible UI.

::code{file="web/app/components/devtools/react-scan/loader.tsx" lines="19-23"}
findings.fixPrompt: In `web/app/components/devtools/react-scan/loader.tsx` line 20, the Suspense fallback is a visible 'Loading devtools...' div. Change it to `fallback={null}` to match `web/app/components/devtools/tanstack/loader.tsx` line 19. This keeps the devtools placeholder invisible and makes the two loaders consistent.

findings.title: Lazy gating keeps devtools out of production
findings.body: The `IS_DEV` check returns `null` before the `Suspense` tree renders, so the `lazy()` factory and its `import()` never run in production. `react-scan` is also no longer statically imported by the root layout, so it is no longer part of the layout's module graph. This is the main intent of the PR and it is implemented correctly.

findings.title: Renames preserve history and the folder structure is consistent
findings.body: `react-scan.tsx` and `devtools.tsx` moved with 100% similarity, so `git log --follow` still works. Both tools now follow the same `<tool>/{implementation, loader}.tsx` layout, which makes the next devtools integration easier to add.

findings.title: TanStack loader now mounts before children
findings.body: The TanStack loader moved from after `{children}` to before it inside `QueryClientProvider`. The devtools render a floating panel, so this should not affect layout or behavior. It is a small change in DOM order, so it is worth confirming in a dev build that the panel still appears above the app.
